claims.statement: Treat Ral Nel as flexible and opportunistic rather than following a fixed build: structure movement and action cards create unusual openings only when objective, map and tech line up.
claims.conditions: The useful line depends on objectives, map, tech and opponent behavior.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 434 beginner guide, published 2025-12-10; rules compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts called the faction roughly B tier but reserved judgment; another host questioned whether versatility offsets weaknesses.

claims.statement: AI Development Algorithm is the safer starting technology in a vacuum because it opens both faction technologies and flexible upgrades. Choose Psychoarchaeology when useful skips make it attractive; Neural Motivator can fish for Overrule, but extra cards can exceed hand capacity and played cards do not enter Data Skimmer.
claims.conditions: Starting choice depends on slice, skips and desired technology path; Neural is a deliberate card-focused alternative.
claims.compatibility: Podcast-era technology discussion; not independently rules checked.
claims.uncertainty: ASR shorthand normalized to known component names.

claims.statement: Plan around the weak home economy: the speakers describe three total resources and limited production, alongside a useful three-influence planet that may fund an early command token.
claims.conditions: Slice wealth and early spending can change the opening.
claims.compatibility: Guide opinion; planet statistics not independently verified.
claims.uncertainty: ASR may garble home-planet names.

claims.statement: Use Survival Instinct as a situational defense or deterrent: after an opponent activates a system containing your ships, it may pull up to two eligible ships from adjacent systems without your command tokens into the active system.
claims.conditions: Most useful when ships are positioned nearby or the map creates a valuable reinforcement window.
claims.compatibility: Ability as discussed in the guide; current rules not verified.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts reported that it rarely affected their research games.

claims.statement: Miniaturization lets ships transport structures without using capacity and place them on planets you control in that system at the end of the tactical action, opening forward placement and structure-objective lines.
claims.conditions: Structures in space cannot use unit abilities; speakers said carried space docks cannot produce during that action.
claims.compatibility: Guide ruling; structures left in space were described as a provisional interpretation.
claims.uncertainty: Rules treatment of unattended structures was expressly tentative.

claims.statement: Consider moving the home dock toward the slice center if forward production repays the risk; keeping it home is reasonable when early plastic needs make moving it unaffordable.
claims.conditions: A forward dock improves reach but can expose home and force ships to be split between defense and front lines.
claims.uncertainty: Speakers differed in their own experience and emphasized the tradeoff.

claims.statement: Use Nanomachines chiefly to place PDS outside normal Construction timing; after useful PDS are out, its action-card exchange is another option. The repair mode was a situational fallback the speaker had not used.
claims.conditions: Each action exhausts the technology; the value is off-tempo structure placement.
claims.compatibility: Guide opinion, not a verified optimization.
claims.uncertainty: Speaker reported mostly using PDS placement.

claims.statement: Linkship can use a transported structure’s space-cannon ability in its system. The episode’s current interpretation rejects copying PDS II’s adjacent-system reach; bring the PDS into the target system.
claims.conditions: The interaction was disputed and the hosts requested later clarification.
claims.compatibility: Provisional guide ruling, not current official FAQ verification.
claims.uncertainty: A different reading would transform the faction’s space-control reach.

claims.statement: Do not assume Experimental Battlestation activates Linkship: speakers’ current ruling was that a dock that may use space cannon does not gain the referenced ability.
claims.conditions: One speaker allowed that later clarification might change this reading.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts expressed more uncertainty here than on PDS II reach.

claims.statement: Linkship II can improve movement and let each Linkship trigger the same transported structure, creating local space control, but weigh it against movement and capacity technologies.
claims.conditions: It remains a space-combat tool and does not solve ground-force delivery; speakers rejected adjacent-system PDS projection as the current reading.
claims.uncertainty: Its reach depends on a disputed interaction; hosts preferred red-blue mobility when tech was scarce.

claims.statement: Last Dispatch can retreat and destroy an opposing ship that lacks Sustain Damage; paired with Watchful Ojz, it can create an earlier exit line.
claims.conditions: The target restriction excludes ships possessing Sustain Damage even if they have already used it.
claims.compatibility: Guide interpretation; combat rules not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: Timing clarification is podcast-era.

claims.statement: Position Alarums near controlled adjacent planets so that after a combat round they can pull up to two ground forces onto their planet, potentially reaching a control objective unexpectedly.
claims.conditions: Requires nearby planets with forces; does not pull from another planet in the same system and cannot chain another mech pull in that window, per the guide’s current FAQ account.
claims.uncertainty: ASR “alarm” normalized to the component Alarum.

claims.statement: Trade for Nano Link Permit as a setup tool: after activation it moves eligible adjacent structures onto controlled planets in the active system, and speakers say the timing lets the buyer build from a moved dock.
claims.conditions: Needs an adjacent structure and controlled planet; buy it before the planned use rather than promising immediate play.
claims.compatibility: Guide timing explanation, not independently verified.
claims.uncertainty: Speakers considered it undervalued and proposed it for Mecatol staging.

claims.statement: Data Skimmer rewards opponents who play action cards during the action phase: while Ral Nel has not passed, their discards accumulate there, and passing lets Ral Nel keep one.
claims.conditions: Own played cards and non-action-phase discards do not enter the pile; value depends on cards opponents spend and when.
claims.uncertainty: Strong cards may be held until late, so the benefit is not guaranteed.

claims.statement: Account for Data Skimmer’s visibility: taking a known strong card can invite Sabotage or change opponents’ timing. Speakers suggested Last Bastion Alliance as valuable protection.
claims.conditions: Public cards make the threat legible to opponents.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts contrasted this weakness with Yssaril’s hidden hand and saw counterplay as a limit on Ral Nel’s ceiling.

claims.statement: Use Kan Kip Rel’s agent to draw two action cards, keep one and give the other to a player whose cooperation or timing you want; the draw also provides a stall.
claims.conditions: Negotiating after seeing the cards may be useful, but the speakers were unsure whether cards can be revealed during resolution and said hand limit is checked after resolution.
claims.uncertainty: Reveal and hand-limit timing were left unresolved.

claims.statement: Watchful Ojz requires Ral Nel to be last to pass, so do not count on an early or automatic unlock; the agent helps with cards but does not guarantee pass order.
claims.conditions: Useful once unlocked, but not an essential engine component.
claims.compatibility: Guide statement; rules not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: Speakers described difficulty unlocking it in one game.

claims.statement: Save Director Nel’s Signal Intrusion for a valuable post-pass action if possible: after the last player passes, unpass and gain two command tokens and an action card; it may open an objective window such as Prove Endurance.
claims.conditions: Speakers also used it simply for the tokens and card; passing stops ordinary turn actions until the hero unpasses Ral Nel, so consider the timing of enemy attacks.
claims.compatibility: Guide interpretation; not independently rules checked.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts had not yet seen the spectacular use they expected.

claims.statement: Treat Ral Nel as a midgame Mecatol or Imperial contender rather than a default custodians faction; build tempo and ground support, and use tradeables to recruit help when useful.
claims.conditions: Space cannon can clear space but does not solve ground combat; the table may deny the point.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts agreed on midgame timing but differed on how much the faction should provide its own punch.

claims.statement: Favor Construction when a second space dock would solve the home production cap and let one dock stay home while another moves forward.
claims.conditions: Pick order matters; following Construction is another route, and Nanomachines does not replace ship production.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts considered Construction especially after Trade or Technology, not a universal first pick.

claims.statement: After round one, consider Warfare for structure and movement tricks, including a Fracture staging plan where Ral Nel lacks a reliable natural setup.
claims.conditions: Even with Linkship II movement, capacity and ground forces may prevent claiming distant planets.
claims.uncertainty: Speakers framed this as a conditional later-round option.

claims.statement: When technology is scarce, favor a practical red-blue mobility plan: Dark Energy Tap, Gravity Drive and Carrier II, perhaps followed by Fighter II or Dreadnought II; add faction technology when the board supports it.
claims.conditions: Movement and capacity solve common problems; Linkship II focuses on space combat and does not carry ground forces.
claims.uncertainty: Players gave alternative lists; this is not a fixed sequence. Hosts agreed green-yellow Breakthrough synergy conflicts with red-blue needs.

claims.statement: Graviton could complement Linkships by removing capacity ships only in the hypothetical where broad PDS II space-cannon reach is accepted.
claims.conditions: Current interpretation in the episode rejects that premise; ground combat remains the stated weakness.
claims.compatibility: Speculative branch, not current legal strategy verification.
claims.uncertainty: High: hosts explicitly tied this tech priority to a disputed interpretation.

claims.statement: Consider Biostims if Nanomachines has multiple useful exhausted modes and a green path fits, since it may let those options be used again.
claims.conditions: Supplemental option only; movement may matter more.
claims.uncertainty: Speaker called it interesting but did not recommend it automatically.

claims.statement: Look for structure objectives as a Ral Nel scoring lane: Nanomachines can place PDS and Miniaturization can reposition structures, making unusual preparations possible.
claims.conditions: Preparation is not scoring; meet every objective condition before claiming the point.
claims.compatibility: Guide advice; objective-specific legality not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Some objective names were ASR-corrupted, so this claim remains general.

claims.statement: Do not rely on a guaranteed Fracture win or surprise action-card victory; the hosts found Mecatol easier to stage because Ral Nel often lacks capacity and ground forces.
claims.conditions: Flank Speed, In the Silence of Space or a forward dock might create an exceptional line, but those tools are not assured.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers had not executed their hoped-for Fracture plan.

claims.statement: Try to stay outside the center of attention and preserve a surprise scoring window, while keeping enough defense to survive after passing.
claims.conditions: After passing, Ral Nel cannot answer attacks until Signal Intrusion; public Data Skimmer cards let opponents anticipate a move.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts called this their preferred posture, not a guaranteed win line.

connections.conditions: Nanomachines places PDS and Miniaturization can later transport structures to controlled planets; this is a placement line, not a guaranteed score.
A transported PDS can provide its space-cannon ability to a Linkship in the same system under the episode’s current interpretation.
The hosts reject transferring PDS II adjacent-system range through Linkship II; this debated interaction would change faction strategy materially.
The agent supplies a flexible action card and stall that can support deal-making and action-card plans.
A buyer can move an adjacent dock into the active system and, under the hosts’ timing explanation, build from it after activation.
Signal Intrusion conditionally reopens the action phase after passing for tokens and a card, potentially creating a late objective window.
Adjacent-system ground forces may be pulled to an Alarum’s planet after combat, potentially helping a control objective when forces are nearby.
